r: Only Congress can create provinces and cities because doing so creates legislative districts; the power to reapportion is part of national legislative power and cannot be delegated to a regional assembly. ARMM’s law creating Shariff Kabunsuan was void.
f: The ARMM Regional Assembly created the province of Shariff Kabunsuan under a delegation in the ARMM Organic Act.
h: The delegation and the creation of the province were void.
x: Use when a body other than Congress tries to create districts or change Congress’s composition.
g: Gatmaytan’s book: an inferior legislative body created by a superior one cannot change the superior’s membership.

r: The power to create local government units is legislative. Absence of a Local Government Code with criteria did not stop the legislature from creating a municipality, subject to a plebiscite.
f: BP 56 created the Municipality of Sibagat before the Local Government Code was enacted.
x: Plenary legislative power except as limited by the Constitution.

n: ABAKADA Guro Party List v. Purisima
r: Once a law is enacted, Congress’s role is limited to scrutiny and investigation. A Joint Congressional Oversight Committee empowered to approve the IRR is a legislative veto: it lets Congress take part in implementing the law, violates separation of powers, and bypasses bicameralism and presentment. The rest of RA 9335 was upheld through the separability clause.
f: RA 9335 (Attrition Act) gave BIR and BOC personnel rewards for exceeding revenue targets and created a JCOC to approve its IRR.
h: The JCOC approval provision (Sec. 12) was void; the reward system and the rest of the law stood.
x: The 2023 midterm (Tax Code Sec. 290-A oversight committee on illicit trade): ask whether the committee merely reviews and recommends (valid scrutiny) or approves, deputizes, or directs implementation (invalid). Also any bicam or law clause requiring congressional approval of IRRs.
test: Valid oversight: (1) scrutiny (budget hearings, question hour, confirmation); (2) investigation in aid of legislation. Invalid: supervision or any post-enactment approval, veto, or role in execution.
g: Gatmaytan’s book treats legislative vetoes as the textbook violation of separation of powers (‘an inward-turning delegation’ attaching a congressional leash). He also criticizes tying severability to separability clauses, citing ABAKADA.

r: A title must not mislead. ‘An Act creating the Municipality of Dianaton in Lanao del Sur’ hid that the law also took barrios from Cotabato. The whole law was void because the valid and invalid parts could not be separated.
f: RA 4790’s body included twelve barrios of Cotabato province in a new Lanao del Sur town.
h: RA 4790 declared void in its entirety.
x: Title and one-subject rule: dual purposes (no hodgepodge; the title must inform legislators and the public).
test: Title rule complied with if the title is comprehensive enough to include the general object, and all parts are germane to it; it is violated if the title misleads or the body includes a subject not fairly embraced.

r: A municipality given power to ‘regulate’ businesses cannot prohibit a lawful business outright; the amending law’s title spoke only of regulation, and a construction that keeps the law constitutional is preferred. The Bocaue ordinance closing all night clubs was unreasonable.
f: Bocaue, Bulacan passed a ‘Prohibition and Closure Ordinance’ banning night clubs and cabarets.
x: Titles limit what a law can be read to authorize; police power by LGUs must be reasonable (regulate, not prohibit).

r: The Fair Election Act’s repeal of the rule that elective officials are deemed resigned upon filing a COC is germane to its title on fair and honest elections; titles are construed liberally so as not to cripple legislation.
f: Petitioners argued that Sections 12 and 14 of RA 9006 were riders unrelated to lifting the political ad ban.
x: Rider and title challenges: liberal construction; germaneness.
